rules.title: How dice pays
rules.lede: The whole game is one public contract. Here is what it does, line by line.

roll.title: The roll
roll.body: Chainlink VRF sends one random number for each bet. The contract turns it into a roll from 1 to 100 for every round, so nobody can pick or redraw it.

line.title: Your line
line.body: Roll under wins on your line or any number under it. Roll over wins on any number above it. Your win chance runs from 2% to 97%; any higher and a win would pay back no more than your stake.

payout.title: The payout
payout.body: A win pays your stake times 100, divided by your win chance, less a {rate} house edge taken from that payout. At a 50% chance that is {pays} times your stake.

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: Bets start at {min} {symbol} a round, and one bet can play up to {rounds} rounds. The most you can stake depends on your odds and on what the house pool can pay out. The slip shows it before you sign.

fees.title: Fees
fees.body: Each bet pays one randomness fee in ETH, plus network gas, and all its rounds share it. Your wallet attaches up to {fee} for it today. Chainlink charges at the gas price when the bet goes through, and the rest comes back in the same transaction.

refund.title: If no number comes
refund.body: If the random number hasn't arrived after {wait}, you can refund your stake. The randomness fee is not refunded.

head.title: Roulette
head.lede: Chainlink VRF picks a number from 0 to 36 and the ball drops into its pocket. Any number under your chips wins.

table.title: The table
table.rule: One bet covers every number your chips are on. Any of them pays 37 ÷ the numbers covered, less a {rate} house edge.

status.ready: Put chips on the layout, then place your bet.
status.all: Your chips cover every number. Take one off to bet.
status.waiting: Waiting for the random number. The ball spins until it arrives.

empty.lead: Put a chip on the layout.
empty.body: Tap a number or a bet on the felt. Every chip adds its numbers to one bet.

all.body: A bet on all 37 numbers can't win more than it stakes. Take a chip off.

head.title: Slots
head.lede: Chainlink VRF picks a symbol for each of the three reels and they stop on it, left to right. Three alike pays; three sevens pays most.

table.title: The machine
table.rule: Each reel stops on a symbol Chainlink VRF picks, every symbol equally likely. Pays include your stake, less a {rate} house edge: on average {back} of stakes come back.

status.ready: Set your stake on the slip, then place the bet.
status.waiting: Waiting for the random number. The reels spin until it arrives.

head.title: Keno
head.lede: Pick 1 to 5 numbers. Chainlink VRF draws 5 of the 15 balls; the more of yours it draws, the more you get back.

table.title: The table
table.paystrip: What each number of hits pays
table.rule: 5 of the 15 balls are drawn. Every number of hits pays something; a faint pay returns less than the stake. Pays include your stake and are per round, less a {rate} house edge.

status.ready: Pick 1 to 5 numbers, then place your bet on the slip.
status.waiting: Waiting for the random number. The balls tumble until it arrives.
status.full: Up to 5 numbers. Take one off to change.

empty.body: Tap 1 to 5 numbers on the board. Each round draws 5 of the 15.

receipt.drewRounds: The last round drew {balls}. Hits by round: {list}.

head.title: Plinko
head.lede: Chainlink VRF decides every bounce: eight fair lefts or rights. The ball pays what its cup says; the further out, the more.

table.title: The table
table.cups: What each cup pays, and how often a ball lands there
table.rule: Every bounce is a fair left or right from Chainlink VRF. Risk changes what the cups pay, never where the ball goes: at every level the outer six cups win. Pays include your stake and are per ball, less a {rate} house edge.

status.waiting: Waiting for the random number. The ball rocks in its cradle until it arrives.

head.lede: Call heads or tails. Chainlink VRF flips the coin; if it lands on your call, you get 1.96 times your stake.

table.rule: The coin is fair: Chainlink VRF picks each side half the time. A match pays twice the stake, less a {rate} house edge.

head.title: Baccarat
head.lede: Back the Player, the Banker or a tie. Chainlink VRF draws every card; the hand closer to nine wins.

table.rule: Every card is a fresh draw from Chainlink VRF; suits are for show. Ace counts 1, tens and pictures 0, and only the last digit of a total counts. A tie loses Player and Banker bets. Pays include a {rate} house edge.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.description: These terms govern access to the ArbiGameFi frontend and summarize the on-chain rules that apply to bets and pool deposits. The contracts enforce these rules; where this page and a contract differ, the contract decides.

highlights.0: The frontend is an interface for public on-chain systems; the contracts decide every bet and withdrawal.
highlights.1: Every change to pools, games and parameters waits at least 72 hours in a public governance timelock and can be cancelled while it waits.
highlights.2: A pause stops new bets and new deposits only. Settlement, refunds, claims and withdrawals continue.
highlights.3: A bet whose result arrives but cannot be settled can be voided: the stake is returned, the VRF fee is not.
highlights.4: Users remain responsible for wallet custody, transaction review, gas, and local compliance.

0.title: Use of the frontend
0.body: The ArbiGameFi frontend presents wallet-native access to on-chain game rooms and bankroll surfaces. Access to the frontend does not remove the need to review transaction contents, quoted fees, network conditions, or the contracts being called before signing.

1.title: Wallets and execution
1.body: Users retain custody of their wallets and private keys. ArbiGameFi does not take custody of wallets, cannot recover private keys, and cannot reverse transactions that have been confirmed by the relevant network.

2.title: Bets and limits
2.body: A bet is accepted only while the pool can reserve its largest possible payout. In the USDC pool every round stakes at least 0.01 USDC, and one bet has at most 25 rounds. A pool holds at most 128 open bets and each player at most 2 of them, so a new bet can be rejected while the pool is full or while two of your bets are still open. When a bet is accepted it fixes its game rules, house edge, referral terms and refund deadline; later changes apply only to new bets.

3.title: Results, refunds and voids
3.body: Each bet requests one random value from Chainlink VRF and normally settles in the transaction that delivers it. If no random value arrives by the bet's refund deadline (one hour by default, never more than one day), anyone can refund the bet. Once a random value has arrived it is never drawn again: the bet settles with it, and anyone can retry a settlement that failed. If settlement keeps failing, anyone can void the bet 24 hours after its request when a void window covers it, or 7 days after its request without one. A void first tries to settle the bet once more; only if that fails is the stake returned as a claimable balance. The VRF fee is not refunded, and a voided bet pays no winnings, even when its result would have won.

4.title: Who decides about voids
4.body: A void window for a pool can be opened by the governance timelock, the operator's Safe or the pool's guardian, and only while a result in that pool is waiting to be booked. Whoever opens it chooses when, after the random values are public; while a failure lasts, the order in which bets are voided decides which ones end first. The operator's keeper attempts every eligible bet in request order and publishes the results. A void needs about 11 million gas: some smart-contract wallets and bundlers cannot send it, but any other account or the keeper can void the bet for you. A void also needs the pool's accounting to balance. If the asset issuer freezes the pool's tokens, a returned stake is paid once the freeze ends; if the issuer seizes or burns them, the accounting no longer balances and bets cannot be voided.

5.title: Pauses and stopped games
5.body: The operator's Safe or the pool's guardian can pause a pool at once. A pause stops new bets and new deposits only: settlement, refunds, voids, claims and withdrawals continue. Unpausing is a governance change and waits at least 72 hours. The Safe can also deactivate a pool or disable a game at once; bets already accepted still settle, refund or void, and a disabled game is never enabled again.

6.title: Governance and changes
6.body: The contracts cannot be upgraded. Every change to pools, hubs, games and parameters is an operation of the governance timelock: the operator's Safe schedules it, it is published, and it waits at least 72 hours, a delay that can be raised but never set below 72 hours. While it waits, the Safe or the guardian, an independent multisig whose signers are not Safe signers, can cancel it; once it is ready, anyone can execute it. A house-edge change then waits seven more days. Governance cannot take LP funds or player balances. If the Safe is lost or gives up its role, no rule can change again and the pools can only wind down: settlement, refunds, 7-day voids and withdrawals continue, and an existing pause stays.

7.title: Providing liquidity
7.body: Each deposit creates its own NFT with a 24-hour withdrawal lock. A pool can take deposits before betting starts: betting begins only after a separate activation has waited 72 hours in the timelock. Once the lock has passed, the NFT's owner can withdraw up to the pool's free capital. LP capital takes the other side of every bet, and earlier and later deposits can share results; the risk disclaimer explains how.

8.title: Protocol and room risk
8.body: Live rooms depend on smart contracts, randomness or oracle providers, indexers, RPC infrastructure, and third-party wallet providers. Service availability and outcome visibility may be affected by any of these layers.

9.title: No universal availability
9.body: The frontend may not be available in every jurisdiction, network condition, browser environment, or release channel. Users are responsible for determining whether access or participation is permitted where they are located. The smart contracts do not check a user's location, age or identity, and anyone can call them directly. The country restrictions, entry confirmation and responsible-gambling tools of this frontend apply to the frontend only. Using the contracts directly from a place where participation is not permitted, or to get around those restrictions, breaches these terms.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: ArbiGameFi is built around public-chain execution. This policy explains the limited data the frontend may process in addition to wallet and transaction data already visible on-chain.

highlights.0: Wallet addresses and transaction hashes may be displayed when they are already public on-chain.
highlights.1: Product analytics and performance telemetry may be used to improve reliability and usability.
highlights.2: Wallet connectors, RPC providers, indexers, and oracle integrations may process request metadata.

0.title: Public blockchain data
0.body: Wallet addresses, transaction hashes, bet states, settlement outcomes, and bankroll activity may be rendered in public room feeds because they are already visible on-chain.

1.title: Frontend analytics
1.body: The frontend may collect product analytics, performance metrics, and engagement signals to improve room layouts, onboarding, operational visibility, and release quality.

2.title: Third-party services
2.body: Wallet connectors, RPC providers, indexers, analytics services, and oracle integrations may process request metadata as part of normal operation. Their own terms and privacy rules also apply.

3.title: Data minimization
3.body: The product should avoid collecting private keys, seed phrases, unnecessary personal identifiers, or raw wallet activity that is not required for product reliability, fraud prevention, or legal compliance.

disclaimer.title: Risk Disclaimer
disclaimer.description: ArbiGameFi presents interfaces for on-chain gaming and pool deposits. Interacting with these systems involves financial, legal and technical risks. This page lists the risks the protocol keeps by design.

highlights.0: Smart contracts, randomness providers, indexers, RPC endpoints, and wallet clients can fail or lag.
highlights.1: LP capital takes the other side of every bet; earlier and later deposits share results, and exits are first come, first served.
highlights.2: A pause never blocks withdrawals, so it cannot stop a defect in the withdrawal path either.
highlights.3: Users are responsible for determining whether participation is lawful in their jurisdiction.

0.title: Protocol risk
0.body: Smart contract bugs, oracle disruptions, delayed finality, indexer lag, wallet client failures, or network congestion can affect the user experience or temporarily affect room visibility.

1.title: Liquidity and withdrawals
1.body: LP capital pays every winning bet. A withdrawal is limited to the pool's free capital, which shrinks while bets reserve their largest possible payouts, and no date for full repayment is guaranteed. While a result is waiting to be booked, deposits and withdrawals stop until it is settled or voided; anyone can void it 7 days after its request.

2.title: Transaction ordering
2.body: A matured deposit can be withdrawn before a bet's result is recorded on-chain if free capital allows. Capital that stays, or arrives later, may then share gains or absorb losses from earlier bets, depending on whether the earlier deposits still cover each bet's largest possible loss. The 24-hour lock does not remove this ordering advantage, and fair ordering of capital is not promised.

3.title: Exits during an incident
3.body: In an incident, withdrawals are first come, first served: an early LP can withdraw in full while free capital lasts, and the remaining deposits carry every open bet. A pause stops new bets and deposits but never withdrawals or XP claims, so it cannot stop a defect in those paths either. The 72-hour timelock lets LPs leave before a change takes effect only if the pool is deactivated early enough and no result is waiting; while bets keep running, a large deposit may not exit in full.

4.title: Governance and the guardian
4.body: Changes wait 72 hours and can be cancelled, but they still depend on the operator's Safe and on someone watching the queue; queued changes are announced publicly. The guardian can cancel any queued change, including its own replacement and an unpause: a rogue guardian can keep a pool paused, which stops new bets and deposits but freezes no funds. If the Safe is lost or gives up its role, governance is frozen for good and the pools can only wind down.

5.title: Voids
5.body: A void returns only the stake: the VRF fee is not refunded, and a bet that would have won pays no winnings. Whoever opens a void window chooses when, after the random values are public, and while a failure lasts the order of execution decides which bets are voided first.

6.title: Pool capacity
6.body: A pool holds at most 128 open bets and each player at most 2, so 64 addresses can fill a pool and turn other players away until their bets end.

7.title: Outcome and settlement risk
7.body: Casino rooms depend on Chainlink VRF. Settlement may be delayed when the randomness provider lags or the network delays transactions; a bet whose random value never arrives is refunded after its deadline.

8.title: Asset issuer
8.body: The USDC issuer can freeze, seize or burn tokens held by the pool contracts. A freeze delays payments until it ends. A seizure leaves the pool's accounting short; deposits, withdrawals, settlement and voids can then stop.

9.title: Jurisdiction and compliance
9.body: Users must determine for themselves whether use of the frontend, room participation, or LP activity is lawful in their jurisdiction. The contracts are permissionless: for bets and for LP deposits alike, they do not check where a user is or who they are. Country restrictions apply only to this frontend. The entry confirmation, self-exclusion and reminders are stored in the browser where they were made and apply only there. None of them covers anyone who interacts with the contracts directly.

items.a: Connect a wallet from the top-right menu, make sure you're on a supported network, and pick a game. Wins pay straight to your wallet — there's no signup, deposit account, or custody.

items.q: How do I get test funds on Base Sepolia?
items.a: Base Sepolia is a testnet. Get free test ETH from a Base Sepolia faucet for gas, then use a test USDC faucet for the play balance. Testnet funds have no real value.

The Bank is the on-chain vault that backs every payout. Before a bet is accepted, its maximum payout is reserved there, and you can inspect balances and reserves on the Pools page. Every win is paid from it.

House edge is the margin built into game payouts. In the current v1.6 design, LPs retain 50% of theoretical house edge calculated from used turnover; protocol fees and referral rewards share the other half. This is not a guaranteed LP return. The project has not launched. Each game shows its applicable rate in Game Info.

Bets settle using Chainlink VRF for provably fair randomness. After you place a bet, the contract requests a random number; once it arrives the round settles automatically. This usually takes a few seconds.

items.q: What if the random number never arrives?
items.a: After the refund deadline you can take your stake back yourself; the refund button appears in the round status panel. The randomness fee is not refunded. In rare cases, such as a USDC issuer freeze, a payment can be delayed; see the Terms.

items.q: How do I verify a bet was fair?
items.a: Every settled round exposes its bet ID, VRF request ID, random hash, and settlement transaction. Use "Copy proof of fairness" on the result screen to export a JSON receipt anyone can independently verify on-chain.

Two things: the game's house edge, taken from a win and already reflected in the payouts shown, and a Chainlink VRF fee in ETH for the random number. The room shows the most your wallet will attach; the unused part comes back in the same transaction. Network gas is extra.

MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet, Trust, Rainbow, OKX, and any WalletConnect-compatible wallet. On desktop use a browser extension; on mobile, open the site inside your wallet's in-app browser or scan the WalletConnect QR.

items.q: Is this custodial? Do you hold my funds?
items.a: ArbiGameFi never holds your funds in an account we control. While a bet is open, its stake sits in the public Bank contract until it settles, and winnings settle directly to your wallet.

items.q: How do I stay in control of my play?
items.a: Open Responsible Gambling from the footer to set a session reminder, record daily deposit and loss limits, or self-exclude for a fixed period. These settings are saved in this browser only. Daily limits are not yet checked when you bet or deposit, and self-exclusion does not apply to other browsers, devices or apps. You must be of legal age in your jurisdiction to play.
